glazed.what: Glazed green ceramic wavy pantiles / S-tiles laid in overlapping horizontal courses with vertical fluted drainage channels; left swatch and right 3D slope look like the same covering.
glazed.culture: East Asian / Chinese imperial or temple architecture (e.g., Ming or Qing dynasty), or Mediterranean glazed tile roofs.
glazed.defect: No visible boundary seam or holes in the tiled swatch, though the right 3D patch exhibits stepped blocky lighting/shadow artifacts across the middle courses.

kawara.what: Dark grey / charcoal ceramic wavy pantiles laid in overlapping horizontal courses with vertical fluting; left swatch and right 3D slope look like the same covering.
kawara.culture: Traditional East Asian (Japanese kawara or Chinese clay tile roofs, Edo period to modern) or European ceramic/slate pantiles.
kawara.defect: No visible boundary seam, holes, or prominent repeating blotches in the swatch; the right 3D patch displays blocky stepped lighting/shadow rendering artifacts.

tongwa.what: Grey ceramic curved pantiles / barrel tiles laid in overlapping horizontal courses with wide fluted troughs; left swatch and right 3D slope look like the same covering.
tongwa.culture: Traditional East Asian (Japanese or Korean tile roofs) or Southern European / Mediterranean pantiles, pre-industrial to modern.
tongwa.defect: Noticeable repeating brownish/warm-tinted blotches aligned across identical columns (e.g., repeating across the 2x2 tiling); minor lighting artifacts on the 3D slope; no holes or cut seams.

tes.what: Wooden shingles / shakes or timber planks laid in overlapping horizontal courses; left swatch and right 3D slope look like the same covering.
tes.culture: Medieval European, Alpine, Scandinavian, or North American colonial / rustic frontier.
tes.defect: Visible alignment/grid defect: vertical board seams line up continuously across courses rather than being staggered, and identical wood grain patterns repeat across the 2x2 tiling; no holes.

sod.what: Green sod / turf / layered vegetative thatch roof laid in overlapping horizontal stepped terraces; left swatch and right 3D slope look like the same covering.
sod.culture: Traditional Scandinavian / Nordic (Viking Age to early modern torvtak) or Celtic vernacular architecture.
sod.defect: Prominent repeating fringe contours along the lower edge of the grass terraces due to the 2x2 tiling repeat; no cut seams or holes.
